name: Antelope
label: Dischord
lede: Three people, one guitar, two drummers who took turns on bass, and seven years of wiry, stop-start music that sounded like nothing else on the label.

eras.title: Two Vertebrates and a Guapo
eras.text: Antelope came together in Washington in 2001 from two scenes at once: Bee Elvy and Mike Andre from The Vertebrates, and Justin Moyer from El Guapo. The setup was the hook from day one. One guitar, and two players who swapped drums and bass between them.

years.h: Moyer, Elvy and Andre start a band with no fixed drummer
years.p: Dischord lists [[Justin Moyer|68cb15fd-5c0c-4b60-ad06-935ac0756a4d]] on guitar and vocals, and both [[Bee Elvy|05615fd4-be3f-489f-aa7c-cc3d14e4c4e9]] and [[Mike Andre|18f336ed-8cdb-4b22-9186-daedae20bf66]] on drums, bass and vocals. Nobody owned the kit; Elvy and Andre traded places.
years.xp:
Bee Elvy and Mike Andre came out of The Vertebrates. Justin Moyer was still in [[El Guapo|be23bf0a-67c6-4b2f-ba2a-89d983f5ebdd]], the Wesleyan-born band that had landed on Dischord with super/system in 2001, and the same year, according to Wikipedia, he was diagnosed with epilepsy, which put his duo project Edie Sedgwick on hold.

Antelope gave Moyer a very different outlet: minimal, repetitive, built on gaps as much as notes.

eras.title: Out on the road with the Dischord class of 2003
eras.text: Antelope's first record was a co-release with Bug Records, and then the band toured with Q and Not U and Black Eyes, two of the most restless groups in the city. By 2004 Ian MacKaye was producing Antelope at Inner Ear.

years.h: Antelope's S/T EP, cut with Trans Am's Phil Manley
years.p: Antelope recorded six songs with Phil Manley of [[Trans Am|7c5acaaa-3f74-4e16-82b2-f8046fce4338]] at National Recording Studios in March 2002. Dischord and Bug Records co-released them as Dischord No. 132.5.
years.xp: The half catalog number marks the EP as a Dischord co-release rather than a full label release.

years.h: Antelope tour with [[Q and Not U|a934e33f-b3cb-47dd-9638-f7f1f25fe162]] and [[Black Eyes|50d90400-e7ea-4465-92a5-404605e51ee7]]
years.p: Dischord's history singles out a September 2003 Antelope tour with Q and Not U and Black Eyes, two DC bands pushing punk toward dance music and chaos while Antelope pushed it toward space.
A two-song Antelope single, recorded at Inner Ear and produced by [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]]. Out as a 7-inch, now out of print, and on CD.

eras.title: One album in the Dischord House, then gone
eras.text: It took five years to make a full-length, and they made it in the house where the label lives. By the time critics were reaching for comparisons, the band was nearly done.

years.h: Antelope's Reflector, made in the Dischord House
years.p: Antelope and [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] produced the band's only full-length at the Dischord House in Arlington in late 2006. It came out in 2007 as Dischord No. 157.
years.xp:
Ten songs, from the title track to "Collective Dream," including "Justin Jesus." TJ Lipple mastered it. PopMatters gave it 7 out of 10, called it "unclassifiable," and heard Prince and Delta 5, staccato grooves and ping-ponging guitar and bass riffs stitched together with short bits of silence.

The same review got the facts wrong, calling Antelope a Justin Moyer solo project. Dischord's credits list three players, with Bee Elvy and Mike Andre both on drums, bass and vocals.

years.h: Live at the First Unitarian Church, Philadelphia, September 11, 2006
yt: Live at the First Unitarian Church, Philadelphia, September 11, 2006

years.p: Dischord's history gives it one line: the band broke up in 2008. Three releases, one of them a full-length.

eras.title: Moyer and Andre, still at it
eras.text: The partnership outlived the band. Moyer kept making records under several names while writing for the Washington Post, and Andre turned up next to him again.

years.p: [[Justin Moyer|68cb15fd-5c0c-4b60-ad06-935ac0756a4d]] and [[Mike Andre|18f336ed-8cdb-4b22-9186-daedae20bf66]] start Puff Pieces with Amanda Huron. The self-titled album lands in 2014, Bland in D.C. in 2016.
